_**Agent (auto-smart)**_

Official rule is harsher than “replay the point.”

**ITF / chair-umpire practice:** crowd noise and spectator **“out”** calls are **not** a hindrance. Point usually **stands as played**. No automatic let just because a fan yelled.

What actually happens:

1. Fan yells “Out!” mid-rally.
2. Player often freezes, thinking it was a line judge.
3. Chair does **not** replay for that. If the other player keeps going and wins the exchange, or the frozen player stops, the frozen player often **loses the point**.
4. Classic case: [Rusedski vs Roddick, Wimbledon 2003](http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/tennis/wimbledon_2003/3021310.stm) — fan “Out,” Rusedski stopped, umpire gave Roddick the point. Duties text: *Crowd noise, “out” calls from spectators… are not considered a hindrance and the point should stand as played.* ([ITF Duties and Procedures](https://www.itftennis.com/media/2509/duties-procedures-for-officials-2026.pdf))

So consequence isn’t usually “fan gets a warning, point replayed.” It’s **you can cost Alex (or the opponent) the point** if someone stops play.

Chair can still ask the crowd for quiet. That’s separate from hindrance.

Draft currently says let / replay / warning — that’s **wrong** for this case. Want me to fix that section to match the real rule?
